subject: Atlas Payments POC: Success criteria & KPIs — follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@atlas-payments.com>, Lila Gomez <lila.gomez@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas Payments POC: Success criteria & KPIs — follow-up

Hi Evan / Lila —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed success criteria for the 2-week POC so we can align before we kick off: 

High-level goal: validate Redwood inference meets Atlas Payments' latency, throughput and cost targets while maintaining quality for transaction classification and routing.

Proposed KPI targets (please confirm priority):
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 200 ms (end-to-end, from request to complete token stream)
- Throughput: sustained 50 requests/sec with 2x concurrency burst (target 100 rps burst)
- Cost: effective cost/token <= $0.02 (including batching) for production-equivalent prompt mix
- Quality: classification accuracy >= 92% on holdout eval set, and <5% regression vs current baseline on key customer flows
- Reliability: 99.9% availability during business hours; error rate <0.5%

Evaluation plan (draft):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize dataset and success criteria -> sign off by Atlas (Evan)
2) Week 1: deploy trial workload to Redwood Dedicated sandbox (baseline run)
3) Week 2: stress and edge-case testing, collect metrics, run evals, final review

Ownership: Jordan (AE) coordinates scheduling and procurement; Marissa (SE) owns setup, runbooks, and metrics collection; Atlas to own eval dataset and business-logic test cases.

Attachments: I attached a short POC plan and our config template. If that looks right, can we lock in a kickoff on Thu 27 May at 10am PT?

Next steps: please reply with: 1) confirmation of KPI targets or changes, 2) dataset owner + link, 3) yes/no for Thu kickoff.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.com]
From: Evan Brooks <evan@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lila Gomez <lila.gomez@atlas-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Payments POC: Success criteria & KPIs — follow-up

Jordan —

Appreciate the summary. High level looks good. A few clarifications/requests from our side: 

- Latency: p95 < 200 ms is our preference, but p90 < 150 ms is higher priority for customer-facing routing. If you can show both that'd be ideal.
- Throughput: 50 rps sustained is fine; please confirm how batching impacts per-request latency for our short prompts (avg 32 tokens).
- Cost: $0.02/token is a hard target for total cost including any overheads; we'll need an example cost calc for a couple of representative flows.
- Quality: 92% accuracy is in line with what we'd accept; we will also supply a prioritized test set (approx 2k labeled examples).

Additionally: data governance — we need to confirm audit logs and retention for the trial; Sam from Security may chime in.

Kickoff Thu 27 May 10am PT works for Lila and me. We'll share the eval set link by EOD tomorrow and loop Sam if needed.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Payments Platform, Atlas Payments
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@atlas-payments.com>, Lila Gomez <lila.gomez@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Payments POC: Success criteria & KPIs — follow-up

Great — thanks Evan. A few operational details from my side (SE playbook):

POC runbook (summary):
- Sandbox: We'll provision a Dedicated sandbox with 2x A100-equivalent GPUs.
- Config: default runtime with KV cache enabled; batching policy set to target 50 rps. I'll share the exact config (redwood-config-template.json) and the sheet with metric dashboards.
- Metrics collection: we'll stream p50/p90/p95 latency, token counts, throughput, error rates; collect cost estimates via token accounting.
- Eval process: run your 2k holdout examples in deterministic mode (no sampling) and report precision/recall + confusion breakdown. We'll also run a 24-hr sustained traffic test to validate throughput and stability.

Ownership & timeline:
- Today (Wed): I will provision infra and drop the config + dashboard link (attached)
- Thu 27 May 10am PT: Kickoff + walk-through (duration 45 min).
- Fri 28 May: Baseline run complete, preliminary metrics
- Mon 31 May: Stress test and full eval, final report out by EOD Tue 1 Jun.

Attachments: atlas-poc-eval-plan.xlsx, redwood-config-template.json

Note on batching vs latency: we will run both low-latency (batching disabled / single-request) and cost-optimized (batching enabled) profiles so you can see the tradeoffs. For short prompts (32 tokens) batching can reduce cost/token by ~30% but may add 20-50 ms of queuing latency depending on arrival patterns. We'll include those numbers in the report.

If that timeline looks good I'll proceed with provisioning and send the Drive links.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Perfect — thanks everyone. Confirming kickoff Thu 27 May 10am PT and that Marissa will share the provisioned sandbox + dashboards ahead of time. Evan — we'll expect the 2k labeled holdout by EOD Wed.

Open items for the meeting:
- Sam (security) attendance to confirm audit log/retention details
- Quick cost calc examples for your 3 representative flows
- Baseline traffic pattern sample (QPS, avg tokens) so we can size batching knobs appropriately

I'll send calendar invite in a minute and include the meeting agenda. Looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Jordan
